full_judgment:
4. The same petitioner filed the above mentioned writ petitions before the High Court Division against the order dated 28.05.2008 passed by the Customs, Excise and VAT, Appellate Tribunal in two separate cases being CEVT/CASE(VAT) Miscellaneous-26/1999 and CEVT/CASE(VAT) Miscellaneous-25/1999 rejecting the respective applications of the petitioner for waiving from depositing the required money as per the provisions of section 42(2)(Kha) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991(VAT Act, 1991) and directing the petitioner to deposit the money as required under the aforesaid section terming those to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 5. In Writ Petition No. 4487 of 2008 giving rise to Leave Petition No. 720 of 2009, it was stated, inter alia, that the petitioner is a reputed cigarette manufacturing company and is running its business with good reputation and is paying VAT regularly and other taxes as per law of the land though it is now in acute financial hardship. The Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT, Jessore, sent four inspection teams to inspect the affairs of petitioner's company from August, 1996 to June, 1997. Those four inspection teams inspected the factory and found that the petitioner generally produce eleven branded cigarette in its factory. They also found that the factory consumes maximum tobacco for production of cigarette during the period and accordingly, they sent their report to the Head Office at Jessore. Thereafter, the Joint Commissioner also went to the factory and inspected the same and gave a report with his comment on 23.09.1999. The Commissioner heard the matter and found the petitioner guilty for evading VAT to the tune of Tk. 17,27,92,042; the Commissioner imposed personal fine to the tune of take 43,19,80,106 and directed the petitioner to deposit the fore along with the evaded VAT. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order dated 06.10.1999 passed by the Commissioner (writ-respondent No.2), the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka; the4 appeal was registered as CEVT/CASE (VAT) Miscellaneous-26/1999, but the Tribunal declined to admit the appeal for hearing without the deposit of 25% of the demanded amount as per the provision of law. Then the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.233 of 2000 before the High Court Division challenging a memo issued by the Tribunal asking the petitioner to deposit 25% of the demanded amount. The petitioner also challenged the provision of section 42(2) (KM) of the VAT Act, 1991. The' petitioner realized that there were some technical defects in the writ petition and the grounds formulated therein were not proper, it got the Rule discharged for non-prosecution on 23.01.2008. After non prosecution of the Rule, the Tribunal restored the proceeding of the appeal. On 07.04.2008 the petitioner filed an application before the Tribunal under section 194 of the Customs Act, 1969 for waiving the statutory deposit stating its present position. The petitioner clearly stated that had been suffering from acute financial hardship and it was not in a position to deposit the required money. The Tribunal hearing the application on 28.05.2008 rejected the same and directed the petitioner to deposit the money within 25.06.2008; hence the writ petition. 

 6. In Writ Petition No. 4488 of 2608 giving rise to Leave Petition No. 721 of 2009, it was stated, inter alia, that the petitioner is a reputed cigarette manufacturing company and is running its business with good reputation and it is paying VAT and other taxes regularly as per law of the land though it is now in acute financial hard-ship. On 10.06.1999, writ-respondent No. 2 issued a notice under section 37 or the VAT Act, 1991 asking the petitioner to show cause as to why punishment should not be awarded upon it for evading VAT. The petitioner gave a self explanatory reply to the said show cause on 23.06.1999 to respondent No.2 denying the material allegations levelled against it. Respondent No. 2 called the petitioner vide his letter No. 4th/A (8) Musak/ Cigarette/Atok/99/1801 dated 08.07.1999 for hearing of the said case on 20.07.1999; the petitioner appeared in that hearing, but respondent No. 2 without considering the actual facts of the case very arbitrarily imposed redemption fine to the tune of taka 10,00,000 and personal fine of taka 27,25,075 and also directed to deposit the alleged evaded VAT of taka 11,23,828.075. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order dated 22.09.1999 passed by respondent No. 2, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. The appeal was registered as CEVT/CASE (VAT) Miscllaneous-25/1999, but the Tribunal declined to admit the appeal for hearing without the deposit of 25% of the demanded amount as per the provisions of law. In the circumstances, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.232 of 2000 before the High Court Division challenging the memo issued by the Tribunal asking it to deposit 25% of demanded amount. In the writ petition, the petitioner also challenged the provision of section 42(2) (Kha) or the VAT Act, 1991. The petitioner realized that there were some technical defects in the writ petition and the grounds formulated therein were not proper, it got the Rule discharged for non-prosecution. After non-prosecution of the writ petition, the Tribunal restored the proceeding of the appeal. On 07.04.2008, the petitioner filed an application before the Tribunal under section 194 of the Customs Act, 1969 for waiving deposit of the required money stating its financial position. The petitioner clearly stated that it had been suffering from acute financial hardship for which it was not in a position to deposit the required money. The Tribunal hearing the application on 28.05.2008 rejected the same and directed the petitioner to deposit money within 25.06.2008; hence the writ petition. 

 7. The main contention in the writ petitions was that as per the provisions of section 42(1)(Ka)(Kba) of the VAT Act, 1991 read with proviso II to section 194 of the Customs Act, 1969, the Appellate Tribunal had jurisdiction to dispense with the deposit as required under section 42(2)(Kha) of the VAT Act, 1991, but the Appellate Tribunal on misconstruction of the said provisions of the VAT Act, 1991 and the Customs Act, 1969 rejected the application and as such, the orders dated 28.05.2008 passed in the respective appeals were liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respective appeals need be heard on merit without the deposit. The High Court Division by a single judgment and order dated 01.12.2008 discharged both Rules relying on the judgment and order dated 25.11.2008 passed in Writ Petition Nos. 4535 of 2007, 4105 of 2007, 4433 of 2007, 4434 of 2007, 4435 of 2007, 4436 of 2007, 4437 of 2007, 3523 of 2007 and 2342 of 2007. 

 10. The question involved in these two leave petitions squarely came up for consideration by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 896 of 2009 and in that case after considering the provisions of sections 37, 42 and 55 of the VAT Act, 1991 and sections 193, 194, 196, 196A, 196B, 196C of the Customs Act, 1969 this Division held that "Therefore, the intention of the legislature is very clear that in order to file an appeal under section 42 of the VAT Act the percentage of the demanded VAT and or the penalty as mentioned therein must be deposited at the time of filing the appeal and in absence of such deposit an appeal cannot be accepted. So, no illegality was committed either by the Commissioner (Appeal) in not accepting the appeal or by the Appellate tribunal in directing the petitioner to deposit the demanded VAT as per the VAT Act and deposit the treasury chalan of such deposit by 18.04.2007 and on the above view the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division was affirmed and the leave petition was dismissed.
